title: Violin
summary: Not yet indistinguishable from a real violin. Pressure comes from a compact receiver and the body's modes stop at 5 kHz. E5 is too dark, A4 sounds cleaner than the recording, B6 does not hold a steady note, and the stopped notes score below the open ones. Four Dominant strings (Pickering's sections), each with two polarisations, drive a computed shell of the Guarneri il Cannone's scanned geometry in spruce and maple, with its enclosed air through an f-hole neck. The bow grips through the friction law measured on real rosin, except on B3, which keeps a Stribeck curve. G3, A4 and E5 use a bow of finite width with hair compliance. Stopped notes press a fingertip on the string with 3.5 N, and carry neither that bow nor the strings' residual flexibility. The open strings are tuned to equal temperament, never to a recording.
physics_present: four strings from compiled Dominant section packs (Pickering 1985), each with two transverse polarisations; all four stay coupled through the bridge while one is bowed

a computed shell body from il Cannone's scanned geometry (Guarneri 1743) with the corrected f-hole shape: Norway spruce (Viala 2020) for the top, bass bar and soundpost, sycamore maple (Sonderegger 2013) for the back, ribs and bridge, 134 modes on the 6 mm mesh
the enclosed air as one cavity through a physical f-hole neck, its conductance from a boundary-element computation of the f-holes
the steady-sliding friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note except B3
a bow of finite width (10 mm in 3 cells) with hair compliance after Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998, on G3, A4 and E5
the exact static compliance of each string's omitted modes at its bridge (residual flexibility), on the open notes G3, D4, A4 and E5
a rigid fingertip pressed onto the string with 3.5 N (Issanchou et al. 2017 contact law), held by a static preload, on the stopped notes B3, B4, B5 and B6
longitudinal string waves and thermochemical room air (N2, O2, Ar, CO2) on A4; dry air (N2 0.8, O2 0.2) as one gas state on the other notes
open strings tuned to equal temperament (A4 = 440 Hz) by a tension factor read from the assembled instrument's own pulse response, never from a recording
physics_missing: a radiating exterior: pressure on every page is the shell's volume and the cavity at 1 m through a compact receiver, with no directivity and no finite receiver
body modes above 5 kHz, and any mesh convergence: every page is on the 6 mm mesh's 134 modes
air modes beyond the one cavity
the strings' tension loss: no printed loss exists for these strings
the string-to-bridge joint's contact mechanics: an authored spring and dashpot per string (200000 N/m, 0.1 N s/m)
residual flexibility on stopped notes: their static preload refuses the row, "released static preload does not include the obstacles' residual compliance", so those cards drop it
the finite-width bow and hair compliance on D4 and the stopped notes
the measured rosin law on B3, which keeps a Stribeck curve (0.8 static, 0.4 kinetic, 0.1 m/s)
friction beyond steady sliding: no rosin temperature and no friction memory
string modes above about 9.6 kHz on the E string, which carries 17 sines, so B6's 5th harmonic has no string mode under it
a player: constant bow speed and force, where the real E5 keeps swelling for about a second after it speaks
one co-characterised instrument: il Cannone's geometry is combined with independently sourced wood and string data
